P1.evidence: No setter notes existed to read back — no setter is referenced anywhere in the call, and the prospect appears to have booked himself off Trevor's videos. Frame was the usual three parts: 'go through where you're at, where you want to go, see if it's actually a good fit' — no 'what's in the way' or 'what you need'. Agreement obtained ('Sounds good?' — 'Yeah, okay') and the open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: Age asked directly ('And how old are you at the moment?' — 36) but height and weight never asked, on a call where the prospect's stated goal is to add muscle mass. Occupation never asked at all — the rep closed a $6,000 offer without ever establishing what the man does for a living. No health-conditions question. Injuries probed well: location, a 1-10 severity scale, frequency and duration ('And how long have you had that for? Like, is that years?'). Diet asked twice and pushed on ('what does it usually look like day-to-day?'). Sleep never asked. Energy asked directly ('How is your energy? Is it very fluctuating?').

P3.evidence: Future-pace ran ('six months from now... how would that be for you?') and produced only 'Nice', so the rep pushed again and got to the kids: 'if I go to the gym, I'm two hours away from them... If I'm there working out, they see, and they learn.' The rep named it — 'being an even better role model'. Good impact and legacy work. But the aesthetics/one-thing question never ran and there was no reflect-back summary ('so this isn't really about X, it's about Y').

P4.evidence: The rep did land one good challenge — 'if you already came to that conclusion like two to three months ago, wouldn't it have been possible to already buy the kettlebells and start doing something?' — which drew out 'Five minutes ago, I could have bought it, but I didn't.' But years of gym training that ended in a cancelled subscription were never unpacked, the prospect never named the structural gap, and the 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own?' line never ran.

P5.evidence: The settle question ran twice because the prospect deflected the first time: 'Do you feel like you're willing to settle for still being in the same position you are in now in the next six months?' and again 'we always get more drive from seeing what happens if we don't do anything.' Line in the sand ran: 'Are you ready for yourself to sort of draw a line?' — 'Yeah.' But the horizon was only six months, not the scripted two years, and 'why not?' was never asked, so the consequence never acquired any weight — which is visible later when $6,000 lands with nothing behind it.

P6.evidence: Both commitment questions ran before the offer. Belief: 'do you feel like when we get all of that in place, you're going to be able to get to the goal of getting more agility, getting more mobility, and also muscle?' Blocker sweep: 'Do you feel like there is anything else that would stop you from getting to the goals... or is it then just putting in the action?' — 'Yeah, just putting in the work.' The best-run phase of the call.

P11.evidence: The main offer was declined and the downsell was made conditional on a spouse conversation and written collateral, so payment and onboarding were never reachable. No link sent, no Trevor call booked, no agreement email.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran cleanly — 'Outside of the investment, do you feel like, yes, I do really want to do this?' — and got a yes. Then one financial-picture question ('what do you usually have left over at the end of the month?'), which surfaced savings and a stock portfolio the prospect said he was willing to draw on: 'I was going to take that, but to put it 6,000 in this training, I think that it's too much.' The rep did not pursue that opening, did not ask about cash on hand, credit cards, available credit or investment totals, and never offered to break the $6,000 up. He left the offer instead.

Three of the six moves ran: the money-aside intent check ('do you feel like, yeah, you want to do this, it just comes down to talking to your wife?' — 'No, I want to do it'), the obstacle probe ('what do you feel like when you explain it to her, do you feel like she would be like, yeah, do it?'), and the would-she-object test ('if she says like, ah, no, you should just try it yourself'). Never ran: 'is this genuinely needing her input or asking permission to bet on yourself', the not-a-joint-decision-like-a-house frame, or the deposit-with-full-refund fallback.

'Let me think about it' was said explicitly at 00:37:20 and the rep went straight to 'Okay' and arranging the email. None of the OA moves ran — no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you there', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no identity close.

SCRIPT GAP — the known 'a cheaper alternative already exists' gap, in its sharpest form yet: the cheaper alternative is Primal Instinct's own product, which the prospect had already found and priced himself before the call. 'I searched online... I thought there was something like $200.' The rep first argued it was 'something completely different', then sold him that exact product four turns later. There is no scripted path for defending the $6,000 tier against the company's own $1,000 tier, and the improvisation actively undercut the main offer.

notes: Phase 6 was textbook and Phase 3 got to the children properly. The call is undone earlier: no occupation, no height/weight, no sleep, no health conditions, and a consequence frame set at six months instead of two years, so there was no accumulated weight to hold a $6,000 price against a prospect who had already found the $200 product online. Coach the OC play to completion — he surfaced a stock portfolio the prospect had already earmarked and walked past it.
